extra.message: User-controlled request body is directly passed to pickle.loads() without validation or sanitization. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload that executes arbitrary Python code (including RCE) upon deserialization.

The host query parameter is directly concatenated into a shell command via os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary commands using shell metacharacters like ; or | in the host parameter (e.g., host=127.0.0.1; whoami).

User input from the expr query parameter is passed directly to Python's eval() function. Even with __builtins__ cleared, a crafted expression can escape the restricted namespace (e.g., via subclassing builtins) and execute arbitrary code.

The XML parser enables load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. An attacker can submit a malicious XML document containing External Entities to read arbitrary files from the server (e.g., /etc/passwd) or trigger Server-Side Request Forgery.

The lane query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without any validation. An attacker can craft a URL like /after/loan-aftercard-069?lane=https://evil.com to redirect users to a malicious site, potentially for phishing.

The server reads the Origin header and echoes it back as Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials enabled. An attacker crafting a malicious origin can get the browser to send authenticated requests to their domain, leaking sensitive data.
The card query parameter is rendered via Jinja2 Template with |safe filter in HTMLResponse. An attacker can inject XSS payloads like directly through the URL.

The fragment query parameter is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and rendered without sandboxing. An attacker can craft expressions like {{ config }} or {{ ''.__class__.mro() }} to access server configuration, environment variables, or escalate to RCE.

The code connects to https://partner.invalid/status with an unverified SSL context. While the URL is hardcoded, this pattern combined with ssl._create_unverified_context() could enable SSRF if the endpoint URL is ever made configurable or if internal URLs are reachable from this server.
A default expr parameter 'amount + fee' with hardcoded values amount=42 and fee=7 is exposed through the eval endpoint. If eval security is bypassed (CWE-95), these reveal server-side logic details.

The pickle.loads endpoint at /bundle/loan-thaw-178 accepts user-controlled input from both request body and query parameters, and wraps with base64 decoding. Combined with CWE-502, this provides multiple attack vectors for RCE.

The name path parameter in /dock/loan-shelf-594 is used directly as a filename via BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name. An attacker can use ../ traversal sequences to write files outside the intended export directory.

The endpoint explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to 0 and Content-Security-Policy to empty string, disabling browser security headers. This undermines protection for any subsequent responses or browsers that still honor them.

The SECRET_KEY defaults to a hardcoded dev value 'dev-only-change-me-for-local-runs' when the environment variable is not set. This means JWT session tokens are predictable in any deployment that does not explicitly configure SECRET_KEY, allowing full authentication bypass.
COOKIE_SECURE defaults to 'false', meaning session cookies may be sent over unencrypted HTTP connections. combined with CWE-798, this makes session token theft trivial.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in Session Cookie Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: GET /api/borrowers/{borrower_id} does not enforce any authorization check for support_specialist or admin roles. These users can read any borrower profile including PII like tax_identifier_last4 and owner_phone by manipulating the ID parameter.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: PATCH /api/borrowers/{borrower_id} explicitly permits support_specialist to modify any borrower profile via the role check on line 1275. After this, apply_profile_update writes all supplied fields into the target profile, allowing modification of PII like tax IDs and phone numbers.

application_detail() exposes internal underwriting notes and full payment account details to all is_staff() users (including support_specialist). However, POST /api/applications/{id}/notes is restricted to admin/underwriter only, meaning support specialists can read sensitive internal financial data they shouldn't have access to.

BorrowerProfile.tax_identifier_last4 and PaymentAccount.routing_last4 store sensitive financial identifiers as plaintext in the database. If the database is compromised, these PII elements are immediately exposed.

cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data

extra.message: Content-Type checking relies solely on upload.content_type from client input. The file content is never inspected for validity - an attacker can submit a malicious executable with Content-Type set to application/pdf to bypass the allowlist.

The database name is interpolated into a raw SQL CREATE DATABASE statement via f-string. While quotes are escaped, all other special characters pass through without parameterization, creating potential for SQL injection if the database name contains unescaped sequences.

DEMO_PASSWORD is hardcoded as 'DemoPass123!' and used for all demo accounts. In any deployment or test environment where this file is committed to version control, attackers can gain full access to every demo account.

GET /api/applications returns all matching applications without any LIMIT or pagination. For admin/support_specialist roles, this query retrieves the entire table from the database, which can be exploited for denial of service via memory exhaustion on large datasets.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits

extra.message: POST /api/auth/register returns HTTP 409 with 'Email is already registered' for existing emails but HTTP 200/201 for new registrations, enabling email enumeration attack. Combined with the password_reset_request endpoint (line 691) returning different messages based on account existence.

The ApiKey model lacks an expires_at field, and no API endpoint exists to deactivate keys. A leaked API key remains permanently valid. The create endpoint (main.py line 1617) only provides the raw_key once at creation.

The borrower_summary field from DecisionRecord is written directly into CSV output without escaping. If a decision records a summary starting with =, +, -, or @, it will be interpreted as a formula when the exported CSV is opened in spreadsheet applications, enabling Excel formula injection.

POST /api/documents/{document_id}/upload writes to UPLOAD_DIR using a UUID-prefixed filename. While the stored_filename uses UUID_{sanitized_original}, the original filename is sanitized with re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]', '_', ...) on line 1018 which prevents path traversal but not all edge cases in stored file operations.

CORS middleware is configured with allow_origins listing specific origins but allow_credentials=True and allow_headers=['*']. While origin filtering exists, allow_methods=['*'] permits all HTTP methods from listed origins with credentials, which could be exploited if legitimate origins are compromised.
